intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

selected_hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the intersection of consumer technology, otaku culture, and innovation that defines modern Japanese tech culture.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and immerse yourself in centuries of Edo-period culture and architecture.

experiences.name: Shibuya and Harajuku Street Food and Fashion Culture Tour
experiences.description: Experience Tokyo's vibrant youth culture by exploring Takeshita Street's quirky fashion boutiques and indulging in crepes, rainbow cotton candy, and matcha desserts. Cross the world-famous Shibuya Scramble and visit Meiji Shrine for a contrast of modernity and tradition.
experiences.location: Harajuku and Shibuya, Shibuya City, Tokyo

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in a world-renowned digital art experience where interactive, boundary-dissolving installations blend technology, nature, and art. TeamLab Borderless represents the pinnacle of Japan's creative tech culture, offering a mesmerizing and fully immersive sensory journey unlike anything else in the world.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check into your boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk to the famous Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner wholesale market is closed but the outer market is open daily). Browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki shops, and street snacks. Get oriented with your neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) for a peaceful evening stroll along the waterfront. Then head to Tsukiji's local izakayas along Shin-Ohashi-dori for a casual welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab onigiri (¥120–¥180) from a 7-Eleven or Lawson convenience store at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of ramen or soba near Tsukiji for around ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Tsukiji — try set meals (teishoku) for ¥1,000–¥1,500. Look for places with plastic food displays outside.

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, subways, and many convenience stores. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 for airport transport. April weather is mild (14–20°C), bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:30–6:00 AM) to experience the Tsukiji Outer Market at its most lively. Enjoy a breakfast of fresh sushi or grilled scallops from the market stalls — this is a quintessential Tokyo experience. Stroll around and chat with vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and anime district. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera, retro game shops, and maid cafes. Window-shop gadgets, secondhand electronics, and tech accessories.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the evening neon lights. Visit a multi-floor arcade (Game centers like Taito Station or Sega) for a few hundred yen of entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh tuna sushi set or grilled oysters for ¥500–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Akihabara: try a curry rice shop (Coco Ichibanya) or a ramen chain for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Akihabara: gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya for ¥400–¥600, or a budget set meal at a local teishoku restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Free Wi-Fi available in many shops. Bring cash — many smaller shops are cash-only. Subway fare from Tsukiji to Akihabara is around ¥180.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa, Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry) — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the backstreets of Asakusa: Kappabashi (Kitchen Town) — a fascinating street lined with restaurant supply shops, realistic plastic food models, and professional cookware. Free to browse and incredibly unique to Japan.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Sumida River for views of the Tokyo Skytree (lit up at night). Enjoy yakitori skewers from street vendors or a standing sushi bar (tachinomi) in Asakusa for an authentic local evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri + coffee) ¥250–¥400, or grab a ningyo-yaki (red bean cake) from Nakamise-dori for ¥100–¥200
meals.lunch: Asakusa: try monjayaki (Tokyo-style savory pancake) at a local spot for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Standing sushi bar (tachinomi sushi) in Asakusa — excellent quality for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free. Kappabashi is free to browse. Skytree observation deck costs ¥2,100 but the exterior view from the riverside is free and beautiful. April cherry blossoms may still be blooming along the Sumida River.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park — one of Tokyo's most beloved public parks, especially beautiful in spring. Explore the park grounds (free), see the lotus pond, and browse the outdoor market stalls. Visit the Tokyo National Museum if interested in Japanese history (¥1,000 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market near Ueno Station selling fresh food, clothing, cosmetics, and snacks at bargain prices. Great for cheap shopping and people-watching. Then explore Yanaka Ginza, a charming old-fashioned shopping street preserving old Tokyo's shitamachi atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Tsukiji base and explore the evening food scene around Ginza (a short walk away). Window-shop the luxury district for free, then eat at one of the hidden budget restaurants in the back alleys of Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area: try a breakfast set at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) for ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market: fresh fruit, grilled seafood, and snacks for ¥500–¥800 eating as you walk
meals.dinner: Ginza back-alley restaurants: look for lunch-menu-style dinner deals or a bowl of tonkotsu ramen for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free. Ameyoko is free to browse. Yanaka Ginza is a 15-minute walk from Ueno. Saturday is busy — go to markets early. Carry cash for Ameyoko vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku and visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) — a serene Shinto shrine set in a forested park. Arrive early on Sunday for a peaceful experience before crowds arrive. Walk the forested path and participate in the traditional coin toss prayer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Takeshita Street (Harajuku) — the epicenter of Tokyo's wild youth fashion and pop culture. Browse quirky fashion boutiques, try crepes from a street stall, and observe the unique subcultures. Then walk through Omotesando — Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées' — for free architecture gazing.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at rush hour. Watch the spectacle from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation area (free). Explore the surrounding streets and department stores.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a convenience store near your hotel before heading out ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Harajuku: crepe from a street stall (¥500–¥700) or a gyoza set at a local restaurant ¥700–¥900
meals.dinner: Shibuya: try a kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500, or ramen at Ichiran (solo dining booths) for ¥980

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free. Takeshita Street is free to walk. Shibuya Scramble is best at 6–8 PM on weekdays but still impressive on Sundays. All subway fares for the day will total around ¥500–¥700.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the free Yurikamome Line scenic ride (or walk the Rainbow Bridge for a unique experience). Explore teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ¥3,200) — one of the world's most innovative tech-art experiences perfectly aligned with tech culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Odaiba for free: visit the life-size Gundam statue outside DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, walk along the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline, and browse the Palette Town shopping complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Visit the free observation deck at Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku (free, open until 10:30 PM) for a stunning panoramic night view of the city.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area café ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Odaiba: food court in DiverCity Tokyo Plaza — ramen, donburi, or tempura sets for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shinjuku: explore Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls serving skewers from ¥150–¥300 each. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a full meal with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless must be booked online in advance. Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free. Yurikamome Line from Shimbashi to Odaiba costs ¥330 one way — consider walking Rainbow Bridge (free) on the way back.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage site with ornate shrines and stunning mountain scenery (about 2 hours from Tokyo). Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (budget option: ¥1,360 one way vs. Shinkansen). Visit Tosho-gu Shrine, one of Japan's most elaborate and colorful shrine complexes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nikko's mountain forests, Shinkyo Bridge (¥300 to cross), and the surrounding temple complex. Walk the cedar-lined avenues and enjoy the peaceful mountain atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo in the early evening. Rest and recover at your accommodation. Grab a simple dinner near Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store onigiri and drinks before boarding the train ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Nikko: yuba (tofu skin) cuisine is the local specialty — try a yuba soba set for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area: simple bowl of udon or soba at a local noodle shop for ¥600–¥900

day_by_day.notes: Tobu Nikko Line round trip from Asakusa is approximately ¥2,720. Consider the Tobu Nikko Pass (¥4,520) if you want unlimited buses in Nikko. The Tosho-gu complex entry is ¥1,300. Start early — aim to catch the 7:30–8:00 AM train from Asakusa.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's coolest bohemian neighborhood, beloved by artists, musicians, and vintage fashion lovers. Browse dozens of vintage clothing shops (many items from ¥500), independent bookstores, and record shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nakameguro — a trendy canal-side neighborhood. Walk along the Meguro River (especially beautiful if late cherry blossoms remain) lined with independent cafés, boutiques, and galleries. This is one of Tokyo's most Instagram-worthy neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ebisu or Daikanyama for an evening stroll through upscale but browsable neighborhoods. Visit Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning bookstore and cultural complex — free to browse) before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa: local kissaten (retro coffee shop) breakfast set for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa: curry rice at a local spot or a sandwich from a bakery for ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Nakameguro: grab takeaway from a local deli or try a casual pasta restaurant for ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best explored on foot — it's a maze of tiny alleys. All attractions today are free to browse. Vintage shopping budget is up to you. Daikanyama T-Site is free and open until midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum area in Roppongi — take the free elevator to the 52nd floor observation lobby for views, and consider the museum if interested (¥1,800). Then explore Roppongi Hills complex — world-class architecture and public art installations, all free to walk through.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) on Odaiba — Japan's premier science and technology museum (¥630 entry). Explore exhibits on robotics, AI, space exploration, and the internet — a must for tech culture enthusiasts. See ASIMO-style robot demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area. Visit the Tsukiji Honganji Temple (free, beautifully lit at night) near your accommodation. Enjoy a relaxing evening exploring the local Tsukiji neighborhood restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery near hotel ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Roppongi: try a lunch special at a local restaurant — many offer ¥900–¥1,200 lunch sets
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area: fresh seafood donburi (rice bowl) at a local restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan (science museum) is excellent value at ¥630 — allow 2–3 hours. Roppongi Hills public spaces and art are free. The spider sculpture 'Maman' outside Mori Tower is a famous photo spot.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji — a neighborhood known for its alternative culture, live music scene, and vintage shops. Very different from tourist Tokyo. Browse the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) and vintage clothing stores that made this area famous.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (¥600 entry) — an outstanding museum covering 400 years of Tokyo history with life-size reconstructions of old Edo neighborhoods. Fascinating for culture lovers. Nearby is the Ryogoku Kokugikan sumo arena — check if there's a tournament (basho) during your visit.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara for a second visit — this time focus on the retro gaming shops, secondhand electronics, and the famous multi-story Yodobashi Camera. Experience the evening neon atmosphere and try a maid café (budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for the experience).

meals.breakfast: Koenji: local bakery or coffee shop breakfast ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Ryogoku: chankonabe (sumo wrestler hot pot stew) is the local specialty — try a budget version for ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Akihabara: ramen or gyudon for ¥600–¥900, saving budget for the maid café experience

day_by_day.notes: Sumo tournaments (basho) are held in January, May, and September at Ryogoku — April may have practice sessions open to the public. Check the Kokugikan schedule. Koenji is a short ride on the Chuo Line.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — a coastal city with the iconic Giant Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu). Take the JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (about 1 hour, ¥940 one way). Visit the Great Buddha (¥300 entry) and the surrounding Kotoku-in temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's famous hiking trails — the Daibutsu Hiking Course connects several temples through forested hills. Visit Engaku-ji or Kencho-ji Zen temples (¥500 entry each). Walk down Komachi-dori shopping street for local sweets and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo in time for dinner. Stop at Yokohama's Chinatown (on the way back) for a brief exploration and budget dinner if time allows, or return directly to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store food before departing ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Kamakura: fresh seafood at the Yuigahama beach area or shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl — local specialty for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Yokohama Chinatown (if stopping): dim sum or ramen for ¥800–¥1,200, or back in Tsukiji for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura round trip from Tokyo is approximately ¥1,880 by JR. Consider a Kamakura-Enoshima Pass (¥1,520) if you want to also visit Enoshima island. Start early — aim for the 8:00 AM train to beat weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Yanaka Cemetery and Yanaka Ginza area again for a relaxed Sunday morning — this old-Tokyo neighborhood is especially atmospheric on quiet mornings. Browse local antique shops and pick up last-minute souvenirs at fair prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Intermediatheque museum inside KITTE building near Tokyo Station — a stunning museum of natural history and art in a beautifully restored post office. Then explore the KITTE rooftop garden (free) for great views of Tokyo Station.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to your favorite neighborhood or try somewhere new. Consider a farewell dinner at a proper izakaya with all-you-can-drink (nomihodai) option for a set price (typically ¥1,500–¥2,000 for 2 hours). Revisit Tsukiji Outer Market for any last food purchases.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka: local bakery or tofu shop breakfast ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: KITTE building food hall: excellent quality lunch sets from various Japanese cuisine styles ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Farewell izakaya dinner near Tsukiji or Ginza: nomihodai set with food orders ¥2,000–¥3,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Intermediatheque is free and closed on Mondays — Sunday is perfect. KITTE rooftop is free. Pack your bags tonight to prepare for checkout. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping refunds at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Wake up early for one last visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a fresh seafood breakfast — a perfect bookend to your trip. Pick up any last food souvenirs: dried seaweed, dashi packs, Japanese sweets, or premium green tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your accommodation (standard checkout is 11:00 AM). Store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at the nearest station. Spend your final hours exploring the immediate Tsukiji/Ginza area — visit Ginza's free gallery spaces or browse the basement food halls (depachika) of Mitsukoshi or Matsuya department stores for gourmet food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Use your Suica card for the train. Claim tax-free shopping refunds at the airport. Enjoy one final bowl of ramen at the airport before departing.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market: fresh sushi or seafood breakfast ¥800–¥1,200 — make it special!
meals.lunch: Depachika (department store basement): grab premium bento or Japanese sweets for ¥600–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Airport ramen or soba before your flight ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transit, check-in, and tax refund processing. Return your Suica card at the airport for a ¥500 deposit refund (minus ¥220 handling fee). Coin lockers at Tsukiji or Shintomicho Station cost ¥400–¥700 for a few hours.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to your Boutique Stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market — browse the fresh seafood stalls, kitchen tool shops, and snack vendors. Pick up tamagoyaki (rolled egg) or fresh oysters from street vendors to get your first taste of local food culture. Stroll to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens for a calming garden walk along Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tsukiji neighborhood at dusk. Head to a local izakaya (Japanese pub) near the market for your first proper sit-down Tokyo dinner. Try yakitori skewers, edamame, and cold Sapporo draft beer in a casual, atmospheric setting.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Street snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, and a cup of dashi broth (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Tsukiji — try Sushi Zanmai or a local yakitori alley spot (budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag is likely. Avoid booking anything that requires advance reservations. Grab a Suica or Pasmo card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April weather is typically mild (15–20°C) with cherry blossom season possibly still lingering.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Japanese breakfast — fresh tuna sashimi don (rice bowl) at one of the iconic breakfast stalls that open at 5–6am. This is the authentic local food experience the neighborhood is famous for. Browse the market vendors selling dried seafood, nori, and Japanese knives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and pop culture district. Explore multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, visit retro game shops, and browse the latest Japanese tech gadgets. Check out the Akihabara Radio Center basement for vintage electronics and components.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening atmosphere. Visit a themed café (maid café experience or a retro gaming café). Walk the illuminated streets of Akihabara at night — the neon signs and electronics displays are spectacular after dark.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — tuna don or grilled fish set at Nakaya or Daiwa Sushi (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500, arrive early as queues form quickly).
meals.lunch: Ramen at a popular Akihabara ramen shop — try Fuunji-style tsukemen (dipping ramen) or tonkotsu ramen (budget ¥900–¥1,400).
meals.dinner: Curry and rice at a Japanese curry chain like CoCo Ichibanya, or a sit-down meal at an Akihabara restaurant serving katsu curry or tonkatsu sets (budget ¥1,200–¥2,000).

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many shops open at 10–11am and close around 9–10pm. The area is dense with content — budget at least 4–5 hours. If interested in retro gaming, the Super Potato store is a must-visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive early (before 9am) to beat the crowds. Walk through the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki cakes, and Japanese souvenirs. Explore the five-story pagoda and surrounding Asakusa Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Tokyo Skytree (15 minutes from Senso-ji). Ascend to the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo — on clear days, Mt. Fuji is visible. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for Japanese food products, tech gadgets, and local design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nakameguro (40 min by subway) for a stylish evening along the canal. Walk the illuminated canal-side path lined with boutiques, independent cafés, and restaurants. This area showcases Tokyo's cool, design-forward culture.

meals.breakfast: Grab a traditional Japanese breakfast set (gohan, miso soup, grilled fish) at a kissaten (old-school coffee shop) in Asakusa (budget ¥800–¥1,200).
meals.lunch: Tempura tendon (tempura rice bowl) at Daikokuya in Asakusa — a historic restaurant that has been serving since 1887 (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).
meals.dinner: Trendy canal-side dining in Nakameguro — try an Italian-Japanese fusion bistro or a modern Japanese izakaya. The area has excellent mid-range options (budget ¥3,000–¥5,000).

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck costs ¥2,100 (book online to skip queues). Nakameguro is especially beautiful if cherry blossoms are still blooming along the canal in mid-April.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku and Meiji Shrine. Start at Meiji Jingu — a serene Shinto shrine set in a forested park. Walk the gravel path through towering torii gates, observe the barrel of sake and wine offerings. Experience authentic Japanese spiritual culture in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's famous youth fashion culture — quirky boutiques, crepe stands, and street fashion. Then transition to the upscale Omotesando boulevard for high-end Japanese design stores, architecture by Tadao Ando, and the Omotesando Hills complex.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Shibuya — a short walk from Harajuku. Watch the legendary Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening hours (6–8pm). Head to the rooftop observation deck at Shibuya Sky or Mag's Park for aerial views of the crossing. Explore the vibrant nightlife streets of Shibuya.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel (onigiri, tamagoyaki sandwich, canned coffee) or a quick café stop in Tsukiji (budget ¥400–¥700).
meals.lunch: Crepes and Harajuku street food on Takeshita Street — try a savory crêpe with egg and ham or a sweet Nutella-banana version (budget ¥600–¥1,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Shibuya — try Ichiran Ramen (solo ramen booths, a uniquely Japanese experience) or a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) like Uobei for a fun, tech-driven dining experience (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free. Shibuya Sky observation deck costs ¥2,000 (book in advance online). Saturdays are busy in Harajuku — arrive at Takeshita Street before noon if possible. Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's most preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Stroll through Yanaka Cemetery (especially beautiful if late cherry blossoms remain), explore the historic Yanaka Ginza shopping street with traditional sweet shops, tofu vendors, and craft stores. This is authentic old Tokyo culture largely untouched by modernization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Ueno Park and the surrounding museum district. Visit the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's largest museum housing samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Stroll through Ueno Park and visit Shinobazu Pond.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji/Ginza area. Explore Ginza's illuminated streets at dusk — window-shop at flagship stores and admire the architecture. Find a local sushi counter restaurant for an authentic omakase-lite experience.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a local Yanaka kissaten or grab fresh bread from one of Yanaka's beloved old-school bakeries (budget ¥600–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the Yanaka Ginza street stalls — try menchi katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet), croquettes, or handmade soba (budget ¥800–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Sushi dinner near Ginza or Tsukiji — try a mid-range sushi counter where chefs prepare nigiri in front of you. Look for omakase sets around ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person for a special but accessible experience.

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum admission is ¥1,000. Yanaka is best explored on foot and takes 2–3 hours. Sunday is a good day for Yanaka as locals are out shopping. Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji (about 15 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for scenic bay views. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book in advance) — world-famous immersive digital art installations that perfectly blend tech culture and artistic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Odaiba — visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue), browse the DECKS Tokyo Beach mall, and walk along the waterfront promenade with views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) for cutting-edge robotics and tech exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via the scenic Yurikamome line at sunset. Head to the Tsukiji area for a relaxed dinner and an evening stroll along the Sumida River.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café in Tsukiji before heading to Odaiba (budget ¥600–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court at DECKS or DiverCity — try a Japanese hamburger steak (hambagu) set or takoyaki (octopus balls) from a food stall (budget ¥1,000–¥1,800).
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near Tsukiji — try a shabu-shabu (hot pot) restaurant or a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) specialty restaurant (budget ¥2,500–¥4,000).

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets MUST be booked online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. teamLab Borderless costs ¥3,200; Miraikan costs ¥630. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a scenic attraction — sit at the front for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with a visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for free panoramic views from the observation deck (open from 9am). Walk through the surrounding Shinjuku skyscraper district to appreciate Tokyo's architectural scale.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Japan's finest parks, featuring French, English, and Japanese garden sections. A perfect midday relaxation spot. Then explore the dense alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls dating back to the post-war era.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Kabukicho — Shinjuku's famous entertainment district. Visit the Robot Restaurant area (or explore the surrounding streets), walk through the neon-lit Golden Gai (a cluster of tiny atmospheric bars seating 5–8 people each, beloved by locals and creatives). Have drinks at a Golden Gai bar for an intimate, culturally unique Tokyo experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Shinjuku café or a morning soba restaurant — try cold zaru soba or hot kake soba as a traditional Japanese morning meal (budget ¥700–¥1,200).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shinjuku Gyoen — pick up a bento box from a nearby convenience store or department store basement food hall (depachika) and eat in the garden (budget ¥800–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Yakitori dinner at Omoide Yokocho — sit at an outdoor grill stall and enjoy skewers of chicken, vegetables, and offal with cold beer or sake (budget ¥2,000–¥3,500).

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free. Shinjuku Gyoen admission is ¥500. Golden Gai bars have small cover charges (¥500–¥1,000) but drinks are reasonably priced. This is a great evening for meeting locals and other travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shiodome and the Hama-rikyu Gardens (near your hotel in Tsukiji) for a peaceful morning. This Edo-period garden features a traditional teahouse on a tidal pond — enjoy matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) in a historic setting. Excellent contrast of old Japan within the modern city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nihonbashi district — Tokyo's historic commercial heart since the Edo period. Visit the Mitsukoshi department store (Japan's oldest), browse the basement food hall (depachika) for premium Japanese food products, pickles, wagashi, and bento boxes. Visit the Coredo Muromachi complex for traditional crafts and modern Japanese design.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji (30 min by subway) — a bohemian neighborhood beloved for its vintage clothing shops, independent record stores, and live music venues. Explore the shotengai (covered shopping arcade) and enjoy the alternative, creative side of Tokyo culture.

meals.breakfast: Matcha and wagashi at the Hama-rikyu teahouse (¥500 for tea set) — a culturally immersive breakfast experience.
meals.lunch: Depachika lunch — assemble a gourmet bento from Mitsukoshi's basement food hall (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a premium spread).
meals.dinner: Koenji dinner at a local izakaya or a small ramen shop — the neighborhood has excellent, unpretentious local restaurants favored by Tokyo residents (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).

day_by_day.notes: Hama-rikyu Gardens admission is ¥300. The teahouse charges separately (¥500). Nihonbashi is walkable from Tsukiji (about 20 minutes). Koenji is best explored in the evening when shops and bars come alive — it has a very different vibe from tourist-heavy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum complex for Tokugawa Ieyasu featuring intricate wood carvings, gilded structures, and the famous 'See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil' monkeys. Explore the surrounding cedar forests and mountain atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Nikko shrine and temple complex — visit Rinnoji Temple and Futarasan Shrine. Walk the stone-lantern-lined paths through ancient cedar groves. If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back in Tsukiji by 7–8pm. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel to recover from the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before catching the train from Asakusa (budget ¥400–¥700).
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine in Nikko — a local specialty. Try a yuba kaiseki set lunch at a restaurant near the shrine complex (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).
meals.dinner: Simple, comforting dinner near Tsukiji — try a neighborhood soba restaurant or a Japanese set meal (teishoku) restaurant (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).

day_by_day.notes: Nikko Tosho-gu admission is ¥1,300. Consider purchasing the Tobu Nikko Pass (¥4,780 round trip from Asakusa) which includes unlimited bus rides in Nikko. Start early — aim for the 7:30–8:00am train from Asakusa to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Roppongi — explore the Mori Art Museum at the top of Mori Tower (53rd floor), which features contemporary Japanese and international art alongside the Tokyo City View observation deck. This is a world-class modern art experience with stunning city panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space with rotating contemporary art exhibitions. The building itself (designed by Kisho Kurokawa) is an architectural marvel. Then explore the Roppongi Hills complex and its public art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Roppongi's famous nightlife district — the area transforms dramatically at night. Visit a rooftop bar for cocktails with city views, or explore the international restaurant scene. This is a great evening for a slightly elevated dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel in Tsukiji or a depachika morning pastry (budget ¥600–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Art Center's Brasserie Paul Bocuse le Musée — a French-Japanese restaurant inside the museum with an impressive interior and reasonable lunch sets (budget ¥2,000–¥3,500).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Roppongi — try a Japanese teppanyaki restaurant or a modern izakaya with craft cocktails. Mid-range dining options abound (budget ¥3,500–¥5,500).

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View combo ticket costs ¥1,800. National Art Center admission varies by exhibition (typically ¥1,500–¥1,800). Roppongi is a 15-minute subway ride from Tsukiji area. Friday evenings in Roppongi are lively — book dinner reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood known for vintage fashion, independent theaters, live music, and a strong counter-culture identity. Browse the dense concentration of vintage clothing stores (furugi-ya) and independent bookshops. This neighborhood perfectly represents Tokyo's creative subculture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Daikanyama and Nakameguro for Tokyo's most stylish afternoon. Visit the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a beautifully designed bookstore complex with curated books, music, and lifestyle products. Browse the boutiques and concept stores along the tree-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Meguro River canal in Nakameguro as evening falls. The canal-side restaurants and bars create a romantic, atmospheric setting. Choose a restaurant with canal-side seating for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Brunch in Shimokitazawa — the neighborhood has excellent independent cafés. Try a Japanese-style morning set (toast, egg, salad, coffee) at a retro kissaten (budget ¥700–¥1,200).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Shimokitazawa curry restaurant — the area is famous for its independent curry shops serving Japanese-style curry with unique spice blends (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Canal-side dinner in Nakameguro — choose from Italian, French-Japanese, or modern Japanese cuisine along the Meguro River. Many excellent mid-range options (budget ¥3,000–¥5,000). Book ahead on weekends.

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is 25 minutes from Tsukiji by subway (via Shibuya). Daikanyama T-Site is free to browse. Saturday is busy in both neighborhoods — Shimokitazawa vintage shops are particularly crowded. Nakameguro canal is one of Tokyo's most Instagram-worthy spots, especially with evening lights reflected in the water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not visited on Day 6) OR explore the Toyosu Market — the world's largest wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market. Book a tuna auction viewing tour (extremely limited spots, must be booked months in advance) or visit the market observation decks to watch the organized chaos of professional fish trading.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ginza for a refined afternoon. Explore the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of premium Japanese stationery and paper goods — a unique cultural experience). Visit the Ginza Six shopping complex for high-end Japanese brands and a rooftop garden. Browse the Sony Park and Sony Showroom for the latest Japanese tech products.
day_by_day.evening: Final special evening — book a kaiseki (traditional multi-course Japanese) dinner or a high-quality sushi omakase experience in the Ginza or Tsukiji area for a memorable culinary highlight. This is the night to splurge slightly on dining.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bakery in Tsukiji (budget ¥600–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Ginza lunch — try the basement food hall at Ginza Six or Matsuya Ginza department store for premium bento boxes and prepared foods (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).
meals.dinner: Special kaiseki or omakase sushi dinner in Ginza/Tsukiji — budget ¥8,000–¥15,000 per person for a memorable multi-course experience. Book well in advance. This is the trip's culinary highlight.

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu Market tuna auction spots are extremely limited and must be registered months in advance. If unavailable, the observation deck viewing is free and still impressive. Sony Showroom in Ginza is free and excellent for tech enthusiasts. Reserve the special dinner at least 2–3 weeks before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit your favorite neighborhood for a nostalgic last walk. Return to Tsukiji Outer Market for a final breakfast of fresh sashimi and tamagoyaki. Pick up last-minute food souvenirs: nori, dashi packs, Japanese sweets (wagashi), matcha powder, and pickles from the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir gathering. Head to Don Quijote (Donki) in Shibuya or Shinjuku for affordable Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and quirky souvenirs. Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for practical Japanese design goods. Return to the hotel, pack, and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — transfer to the airport. Allow 2–3 hours before flight for check-in and immigration. Enjoy one final Japanese meal at the airport — Narita and Haneda airports both have excellent food options including ramen, sushi, and tonkatsu.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji breakfast — fresh tuna don, tamagoyaki, and miso soup at the Outer Market (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500). Savor it.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snack while shopping — convenience store bento or a quick bowl of udon (budget ¥600–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — treat yourself to a proper ramen or soba bowl at one of the airport restaurants before your flight (budget ¥1,200–¥2,000).

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer: Narita is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–40 minutes. Purchase any remaining Suica card balance refund at the airport. Pack food souvenirs carefully — some fresh items may not be permitted through customs. Japan's 10% consumption tax can be refunded at airport tax-free counters for qualifying purchases made during the trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the Tsukiji boutique hotel and freshen up. Take a relaxed orientation stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market lanes to get acquainted with the neighborhood — browse the famous tamagoyaki shops, dried seafood stalls, and kitchen tool vendors at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo with a refined omakase dinner at a top-tier sushi counter near Tsukiji or Ginza. Recommended: Sushi Saito (reservation required well in advance) or Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars, Ginza, 10-minute taxi). Let the chef guide you through the seasonal tasting menu with sake pairings.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or light snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Light ramen or soba at a quality noodle shop near Tsukiji upon arrival — try Tsukiji Kagura for handmade soba
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Saito — expect 20–30 courses of Edomae-style sushi; budget ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real — keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Pre-book airport limousine or private car service. Omakase reservations must be made months ahead; use a concierge service like Tableall or Coveted Tables if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — join a premium guided food tour starting around 8:00 AM. Sample fresh uni, otoro sashimi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and Japanese pickles from legendary stalls. Visit Daiwa Sushi in the outer market for a quick tuna bowl.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza (5-minute walk or taxi from Tsukiji) for a deep dive into Japanese luxury culture. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (9 floors of Japanese craftsmanship), explore the Sony Park interactive tech installation, and browse Ginza Six's high-end retail and art gallery on the rooftop.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ginza Kojyu (3 Michelin stars) for exquisite kaiseki cuisine — a multi-course Japanese haute cuisine experience celebrating seasonal ingredients. Pair with premium sake or a curated wine list.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour snacks — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood, and Japanese street bites count as breakfast
meals.lunch: Tuna rice bowl (maguro don) at Tsukiji Hongwanji area; try Tsukiji Tama Sushi for a premium chirashi bowl
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Ginza Kojyu — 12-course seasonal tasting menu; budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant between 8–11 AM. Book the food tour through a premium operator such as Arigato Japan or a private guide. Ginza Six rooftop garden is a lovely spot to watch the Tokyo skyline at dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (10-minute walk from Tsukiji) — a stunning 17th-century feudal garden with a tidal pond, seasonal cherry blossoms or spring flowers, and a traditional teahouse (Nakajima no Ochaya) where you can enjoy matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) while overlooking the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Sumida River cruise from Hamarikyu to Asakusa — a scenic 40-minute boat ride through old Tokyo. Explore Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, and the Nakamise shopping street. Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for panoramic views. Browse artisan craft shops in Kappabashi (Kitchenware Town) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Asakusa at Komagata Maekawa — a historic restaurant serving traditional Tokyo-style eel (unaju) in a beautifully preserved building dating to 1903. Follow with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Skytree.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or matcha and wagashi at Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse in Hamarikyu Gardens
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa — a legendary 120-year-old institution serving crispy Edo-style tempura
meals.dinner: Traditional unagi (eel) kaiseki at Komagata Maekawa; budget ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens opens at 9:00 AM; entry fee ¥300. The Sumida River cruise tickets can be purchased at the garden's pier — book in advance on busy days. Senso-ji is free to enter but can be crowded; early morning or evening visits are more serene.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and global hub of tech culture. Start with a private guided tour of the district's multi-floor electronics megastores: Yodobashi Camera Akiba and Bic Camera. Explore retro game shops, anime figure stores, and underground maid café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo Anime Center and the interactive Gundam Café. Head to the Super Potato retro gaming shop for vintage consoles. Then visit the Akihabara branch of the teamLab digital art collective for an immersive tech-art experience. Alternatively, visit the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda creative space.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Ginza or Marunouchi for dinner. Reserve a table at Esquisse (2 Michelin stars, Ginza) — a Franco-Japanese fine dining restaurant with an extraordinary wine cellar and seasonal tasting menus that blend French technique with Japanese ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium coffee and pastry at Sarutahiko Coffee in Akihabara
meals.lunch: Akihabara food hall experience — visit the Yodobashi Akiba basement food court for high-quality ramen, katsu curry, or bento; or try Kanda Yabu Soba nearby for century-old soba noodles
meals.dinner: Franco-Japanese tasting menu at Esquisse, Ginza — 8-course menu; budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Saturdays can be very busy — arrive early. teamLab exhibitions require advance booking online. Consider hiring a local otaku culture guide for insider access to hidden shops and collector items.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art spaces on the 53rd floor with sweeping city views. Combine with the Tokyo City View observation deck. The museum often hosts world-class international and Japanese contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle: walk to the National Art Center Tokyo (largest exhibition space in Japan, stunning Kisho Kurokawa-designed building) and the Suntory Museum of Art in Tokyo Midtown. Browse the Midtown luxury mall and the 21_21 Design Sight museum — a design museum co-founded by Issey Miyake.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin (3 Michelin stars, Roppongi) — arguably one of Japan's most innovative kaiseki restaurants, where chef Seiji Yamamoto uses cutting-edge techniques to reimagine traditional Japanese cuisine. An unmissable culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit a high-end bakery such as Viron in Shibuya or Maison Landemaine Tokyo
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Art Center's brasserie or a quick premium bento from Midtown's food hall
meals.dinner: Innovative kaiseki at Nihonryori Ryugin — 15+ course tasting menu; budget ¥60,000–¥90,000 per person; book months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on most days — evening visits offer spectacular illuminated city views. The art triangle walk between Mori, National Art Center, and Suntory Museum takes about 20–30 minutes on foot. Book Ryugin reservations through their official site or a concierge service.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shibuya — start at the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing (best viewed from Shibuya Sky observation deck on the 46th floor of Scramble Square). Visit the interactive teamLab Planets in nearby Toyosu (20-minute taxi) — a walk-through digital art museum with immersive water and light installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the trendy Daikanyama and Nakameguro neighborhoods. Visit Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning architectural bookstore and lifestyle complex) and browse the high-concept boutiques along Nakameguro's canal — especially beautiful in April with cherry blossoms lining the Meguro River.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège (2 Michelin stars, Aoyama) — a progressive French restaurant with a theatrical open kitchen where chef Hiroyasu Kawate creates bold, ingredient-driven cuisine with a Japanese soul. One of the most exciting restaurants in Asia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee at Onibus Coffee in Nakameguro
meals.lunch: Casual but quality lunch at Log Road Daikanyama — try Spring Valley Brewery Tokyo for craft beer and Japanese pub food, or Ivy Place for a garden-terrace brunch
meals.dinner: Progressive French-Japanese at Florilège — 9-course tasting menu; budget ¥35,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets in Toyosu requires advance online booking — tickets sell out weeks ahead. Shibuya Sky observation deck also requires timed entry tickets. The Nakameguro canal is spectacular during cherry blossom season (early April); by mid-April petals may still be falling.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (if still operating at new Azabudai Hills location, check current status). Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and the life-size Gundam statue. Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom for a cutting-edge look at Japanese automotive innovation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) — Japan's premier science and technology museum featuring ASIMO robots, interactive space exploration exhibits, and a stunning globe display of real-time Earth data. A must for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Dinner at Sushi Sho in Yotsuya (if reservations secured) — a legendary 10-seat sushi counter considered among the world's finest, or alternatively dine at Saito (Azabu-Juban) for premium nigiri. Follow dinner with drinks at the New York Bar in the Park Hyatt Shinjuku (Lost in Translation fame) — 52nd floor views and live jazz.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store premium breakfast — Japanese 7-Eleven and Lawson offer surprisingly high-quality onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods
meals.lunch: Lunch at Odaiba's Aqua City food court or the upscale Decks Tokyo Beach mall — try a premium ramen restaurant or Japanese BBQ (yakiniku)
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sushi Sho or Saito; budget ¥40,000–¥70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome automated monorail from Shimbashi — a scenic elevated ride over Tokyo Bay. Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays — if so, substitute with a visit to the Panasonic Center Tokyo or Sony showroom in Odaiba. Confirm teamLab Borderless location as it relocated in 2024.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing over 110,000 artifacts including samurai swords, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculptures, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Book a premium guided tour for deeper cultural context. Stroll through Ueno Park afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods that survived both the 1923 earthquake and WWII bombings. Walk the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (old-fashioned shopping street), visit independent artisan workshops, traditional craft shops, and the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery with its cherry trees.
day_by_day.afternoon_extra: Visit the Nezu Shrine — a stunning vermilion torii gate tunnel shrine less visited than Fushimi Inari but equally beautiful, surrounded by azalea gardens in full bloom in April.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kanda (1 Michelin star, Azabu) — a refined kaiseki restaurant in a beautifully restored machiya townhouse where chef Hiroyuki Kanda serves deeply seasonal Japanese cuisine with an extraordinary sake collection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Kayaba Coffee in Yanaka — a beautifully preserved 1938 kissaten (old-style café) serving classic Japanese morning sets
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hantei in Nezu — a magnificent 6-story wooden Meiji-era building serving kushiage (deep-fried skewers) in a stunning historical setting
meals.dinner: Seasonal kaiseki at Kanda — 12-course tasting menu; budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum's Honkan (main hall) and the Gallery of Horyuji Treasures are the highlights. Audio guides available in English. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Nezu Shrine's azalea garden (Otome Inari) typically peaks in late April.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets (Toyosu) if not already visited, or explore the Azabudai Hills development — Tokyo's newest luxury district opened in 2023, featuring the Mori JP Tower, Azabudai Hills Gallery (cutting-edge contemporary art), and a curated collection of international restaurants and boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando — visit the Omotesando Hills mall (designed by Tadao Ando) for luxury Japanese and international brands. Walk the tree-lined Omotesando boulevard. Visit the Prada Aoyama building (Herzog & de Meuron architecture) and the Louis Vuitton Omotesando store. Explore the Meiji Shrine forest for a peaceful nature break.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at L'Effervescence (2 Michelin stars, Nishi-Azabu) — chef Shinobu Namae's extraordinary restaurant blending French philosophy with Japanese ingredients and sustainability principles. One of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Dominique Ansel Bakery Tokyo in Omotesando for premium pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Omotesando Hills or nearby — try Anniversaire Café for a garden terrace lunch, or Aux Bacchanales for a classic Parisian-style brasserie experience
meals.dinner: Innovative French-Japanese at L'Effervescence — 9-course tasting menu; budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter and the forested approach (Omotesando avenue of trees) is deeply calming. Harajuku's Takeshita Street offers a wild contrast — the epicenter of Japanese youth fashion and pop culture. Azabudai Hills is a 10-minute taxi from Omotesando.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day excursion to Kawaguchiko (Lake Kawaguchi) — one of the Fuji Five Lakes at the base of Mount Fuji, approximately 90 minutes from Tokyo by direct bus from Shinjuku. Enjoy views of Mt. Fuji reflected in the lake (weather permitting in April). Visit Chureito Pagoda for the iconic five-story pagoda and Fuji view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kawaguchiko area — visit the Kubota Itchiku Art Museum (extraordinary kimono textile art in a stunning lakeside museum) and take a short cruise on the lake. Return to Tokyo by late afternoon via direct bus or private car.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Quintessence (3 Michelin stars, Shirokanedai) — chef Shuzo Kishida's legendary French restaurant where a single tasting menu is served each evening, representing the pinnacle of classical French cuisine in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — buses from Shinjuku depart from 7:00 AM
meals.lunch: Lunch at a lakeside restaurant in Kawaguchiko — try Kawaguchiko Hoto Fudo for the regional Yamanashi specialty hoto noodle stew in a dramatic thatched-roof building
meals.dinner: Classical French tasting menu at Quintessence — single menu format; budget ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person; book months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — April mornings tend to offer the clearest views before afternoon clouds develop. Check the Fuji webcam the night before. A private car hire for the Fuji excursion (¥80,000–¥120,000 for the day) offers more flexibility than the bus. Quintessence has very limited seats — reservations are extremely difficult.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Future Park or the Digital Art Museum (confirm current location). Alternatively, explore the newly opened Toranomon Hills Station Tower — one of Tokyo's most ambitious architectural and cultural developments. Visit the Toranomon Hills observation deck for panoramic views and explore the food and retail complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinjuku exploration — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free entry, 202m high). Explore the East Garden of the Imperial Palace (free, beautiful Japanese garden). Then head to Shinjuku for the Golden Gai district — a labyrinth of over 200 tiny bars, each with its own distinct personality — a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon_extra: Visit Isetan Shinjuku department store — Japan's most celebrated department store, especially the basement food hall (depachika) which is a world-class gourmet experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa (2 Michelin stars, Minami-Aoyama) — chef Yoshihiro Narisawa's groundbreaking 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' that draws inspiration from Japan's forests, mountains, and seas. Consistently ranked among the world's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit the Isetan Shinjuku depachika for premium Japanese breakfast items — wagashi, fresh pastries, premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building area or Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square food hall — excellent ramen, soba, or Japanese curry options
meals.dinner: Innovative Satoyama cuisine at Narisawa — 12-course tasting menu; budget ¥45,000–¥65,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Golden Gai is best experienced in the evening before dinner for a pre-dinner cocktail in one of its atmospheric tiny bars — each seats only 5–8 people. The Isetan Shinjuku basement food hall is open until 20:00 and is one of the finest food halls in the world. Narisawa requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury tea ceremony and cultural immersion experience — book a private tea ceremony at Urasenke (one of the three main tea schools) or at a high-end tea house such as Happo-en Garden in Shirokanedai. This 90-minute private experience includes a full explanation of wabi-sabi philosophy, matcha preparation, and seasonal wagashi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Museum in Aoyama — a world-class collection of Asian art in a stunning building designed by Kengo Kuma, with a beautiful bamboo-lined garden. Explore the nearby Aoyama Cemetery for a peaceful spring walk among the cherry trees. Then visit the Comme des Garçons flagship store and the Spiral Building for Japanese contemporary design.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury dinner — reserve at Joel Robuchon Tokyo (3 Michelin stars, Ebisu) — the flagship of the late Joël Robuchon's empire in Japan, set in a stunning château-style building in Yebisu Garden Place. The ultimate French fine dining experience in Tokyo, with one of the finest wine cellars in Asia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium Japanese morning set at a traditional kissaten
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Nezu Museum café overlooking the garden — elegant sandwiches and sweets in a serene setting
meals.dinner: Grand French tasting menu at Joel Robuchon Tokyo — 15-course menu; budget ¥80,000–¥120,000 per person with wine pairing; one of Tokyo's most special dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: The Happo-en Garden tea ceremony can be booked through the hotel concierge and includes access to the beautiful Japanese garden — particularly lovely in spring. The Nezu Museum garden is one of Tokyo's hidden gems. Joel Robuchon Tokyo requires formal attire and reservations made well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — return to Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell breakfast, savoring fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and seafood one last time. Pick up premium Japanese food souvenirs: high-grade matcha, wagashi, premium dashi, or artisan soy sauce. Visit the nearby Nihonbashi area — Tokyo's historic commercial heart — for last-minute luxury shopping at Coredo Muromachi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi flagship store (Japan's oldest department store, founded 1673) for premium gift shopping: Japanese whisky, ceramics, lacquerware, or textiles. Alternatively, enjoy a final tea break at Sakurai Japanese Tea Experience in Minami-Aoyama — a premium tea bar with rare single-origin Japanese teas.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to airport. Depart Tokyo with memories of one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market farewell feast — fresh uni, otoro, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood
meals.lunch: Premium bento box from Nihonbashi Takashimaya or Mitsukoshi food hall — perfect for the airport or flight
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Haneda or Narita — both airports have excellent restaurant options including premium sushi bars and ramen counters in the international terminal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours before international flight departure for airport transfer and check-in. Haneda Airport (HND) is closer to central Tokyo (30–40 minutes); Narita (NRT) requires 60–90 minutes. Purchase Narita Express or arrange private car in advance. Duty-free shopping at both airports is excellent — Japanese whisky, cosmetics, and food items make ideal final purchases. Japan's consumption tax (currently 10%) is refundable on purchases over ¥5,000 at participating stores with your passport.
